core_obligations: Unwind the lifting problem: translate the solid diagram into the elements x_i in degree n-1 with the compatibility relations and y in degree n with d_i y = f(x_i), and state the goal (source lines 6030-6042).
Reduce to the kernel: use termwise surjectivity to subtract a lift of y, obtaining y = 0 and f(x_i) = 0, so that one may replace X by the kernel of f and Y by 0 (source lines 6044-6048).
Conclude: in the reduced case the assertion is exactly the statement that a simplicial group is a Kan complex (source lines 6049-6050).

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-surjection-simplicial-abelian-groups-kan at source lines 6022-6027: a termwise surjective homomorphism f : X to Y of simplicial abelian groups is a Kan fibration of simplicial sets. The proof at source lines 6029-6051 unwinds the horn-lifting problem into the data x_0, ..., x-hat-k, ..., x_n in degree n-1 and y in degree n satisfying the compatibility relations, uses termwise surjectivity to subtract a lift of y and thereby reduce to the case y = 0 (so that X may be replaced by the kernel of f and Y by 0), and then quotes that every simplicial group is a Kan complex. It is the non-trivial-Kan companion of the quasi-isomorphism criterion and needs no exactness input at all, which is what makes the reduction so short.
